column2: Praise with an ulterior motive — a compliment carrying a small business plan behind its back.
The warmest season of the year, when the promise to 'just lie on the beach' mysteriously ends with sand inside every pocket.
A woodland spirit of Slavic folklore who rules the thicket and delights in leading hikers astray — the original forest quest designer.
A deep-bodied freshwater fish prized by anglers and a frequent star of 'they were biting brilliantly' stories.
Someone who deliberately bends the truth, whose hardest job is remembering which version he told to whom.
A long, woody climbing vine that scales rainforest trees without a harness, ropes or annual leave.
The person guiding the group and making the calls — the one who points the way instead of asking where everyone's going.
A computer display screen — your window into the digital world, occasionally reflecting only your own tired face.
A sweet alcoholic spirit flavoured with fruit, herbs, spices or cream — essentially a dessert that decided to become a drink.
An elegant flowering plant with large, trumpet-shaped blooms that looks overdressed even in a cottage flowerbed.
A shallow coastal lagoon at a river's mouth, cut off from the sea by a sandbar — water that hasn't decided if it's a river or an ocean.
A fixed upper boundary or allowance — the line where the system politely announces, 'That's quite enough for today.'
A bright yellow citrus fruit whose sour juice can make a human face cycle through seven emotions in one second.
A clear bodily fluid patrolling the immune system — the body's quiet internal cleaning and delivery crew.
A poet or songwriter who captures feelings in verse and can find a rhyme even while queuing for bread.
A clever, bushy-tailed canine famed in folklore for outsmarting everyone near the chicken coop.
A single character of the alphabet, or an identifying mark used to keep large objects from getting mixed up.
A lightweight alkali metal powering modern batteries so your phone can outlast your attention span.
A metric unit of volume equal to one cubic decimetre — equally familiar to milk cartons, petrol pumps and giant soup pots.
Shaping metal or plaster by pouring molten liquid into a mould — manufacturing that starts off dangerously hot.
A mechanical cabin carrying people between floors, sparing your knees while occasionally testing your patience.
A secondary school or academic institution with a specialised programme — where lessons outnumber break times.
The front of a person's head, housing eyes, nose and mouth — the one ID card you can't accidentally leave at home.
A small watercraft where the instruction 'keep your balance' suddenly carries real consequences.
A deliberate untruth — a story that requires constant sequels just to keep from unravelling.
A flexible climbing stem of a grape plant, responsible for both woven baskets and Friday night's wine.
A ringlet or spiral lock of hair — a single rebellious strand capable of ruining an otherwise sleek hairstyle.
A long training rein used to guide a horse in circles — safety backup for those not quite ready for solo flight.
A sheltered inner space or embrace — a slightly poetic word for comfort, nature's lap or a mother's arms.
A hereditary or life peer of the British nobility — a title that makes even 'pass the salt' sound terribly grand.
Outer shine, refinement and immaculate grooming — the glossy finish occasionally hiding plain exhaustion.
A massive forest deer sporting broad, palm-shaped antlers — looking as though nature issued it a slightly oversized collar.
A shallow, rimmed container or platter trusted to carry everything from the kitchen in a single risky trip.
An aquatic plant whose pristine blossoms rise effortlessly out of muddy waters.
A nautical manual detailing coastlines, depths and hazards so ships don't have to find shallow reefs by feel.
The hybrid offspring of a stallion and a female donkey — a close cousin to the mule.
An open field carpeted with wild grasses and flowers that smells wonderful without ever needing a vacuum cleaner.
A small pool of rainwater that materialises precisely where you planned to step in brand-new shoes.
Earth's natural satellite, faithfully reflecting sunlight and providing free atmosphere for evening strolls.
A small circular hole drilled into a frozen lake by optimistic winter anglers.
A slender bird of prey that glides low over open marshes and fields on patrol.
A framed convex lens that turns a harmless speck of dust into a prime suspect.
A narrow beam of light, or a geometric half-line with a starting point and no destination.
A long, narrow runner strapped to a boot for gliding over snow — forcing your legs to cooperate in unfamiliar directions.
The fibrous inner bark of a lime tree, traditionally woven into mats, ropes and rustic peasant shoes.
Deep affection, care and devotion — the state in which someone else's happiness matters every bit as much as your own.
A covered opening leading into a ship's hold, attic or underground utility tunnel.
A tall garden perennial with colourful spires of flowers and palm-shaped leaves that quietly enriches the soil.
A bright yellow meadow wildflower — a cheerful speck of sunshine best admired rather than eaten.
A pear-shaped Renaissance stringed instrument with a bent neck — the guitar's courtly ancestor.
A slight gap or looseness between mechanical parts — the telltale wobble that tells a mechanic something needs tightening.
A harsh, ringing metallic crash — the unmistakable soundtrack of heavy iron gates or clumsy DIY.
A sturdy strip of leather or webbing that takes the weight of a heavy rucksack off your hands.
A sorcerer or stage illusionist specialising in miracles without ever being asked for a licence.
Rituals, spells and sleight of hand promising to bend the laws of physics on request.
Molten rock churning beneath the Earth's crust — a geological soup impatient to reach the surface.
A bright, cheerful musical key — or, in slang, a wealthy young show-off with expensive habits.
A single sweep of a loaded paintbrush across canvas — one tiny gesture on the way to a masterpiece.
A heavy, dark petroleum residue used in ships and boilers — guaranteed to ruin a white shirt on contact.
A smooth medicinal cream rubbed onto skin — pharmacy relief that saves you from swallowing a pill.
A tall cereal crop bearing golden cobs, equally happy in a farmer's field or a cinema popcorn bucket.
A senior army officer rank — someone who no longer has to prove he knows how to give orders.
A vibrant red wildflower whose tiny seeds add crunch to bakery rolls.
A miniature three-dimensional replica built to test a building, ship or aircraft before meeting full-sized bills.
A tradesperson who coats walls and ceilings, changing a room's colour while permanently decorating his own overalls.
The woman who raised you — uniquely gifted at finding lost keys faster than the person who misplaced them.
A fast, highly venomous African snake — definitely not a reptile you want to challenge to a race.
A juicy, fragrant tropical fruit best eaten over a sink with plenty of napkins on standby.
An enclosed ring for horse riding, circus acts or training — a space built for learning to stay inside the lines.
An intense, consuming obsession — or, in psychiatry, a state of abnormally elevated energy and mood.
Miraculous food sent from heaven in the wilderness — every hungry traveller's dream of takeaway delivery.
A large Siberian red deer prized for its branching antlers and unhurried forest stride.
A loosely woven cotton fabric used for medical dressings — remarkably useful despite being mostly holes.
The fourth planet from the Sun, famous for rusty red dust and humanity's long-standing plans to move there.
A covering worn over the face for protection or disguise — letting you stay mysterious until someone recognises your shoes.
Skilled kneading of muscles and soft tissue — the only socially acceptable way to lie down while someone else works.
An edible woodland mushroom with a glossy, sticky brown cap commonly found beneath pine trees.
A member of an ancient fraternal order rich in symbols, rituals and endless conspiracy theories.
One of the four categories in a deck of playing cards, or a matching jacket and trousers.
The abstract science of numbers, shapes and patterns — proving that even infinity has to follow rules.
The operator sitting at the controls of a locomotive, responsible for keeping the timetable honest.
A competitive sporting fixture between two rivals or teams, or a tiny wooden stick that strikes a flame.
A secretive organised crime syndicate — or the classic party game where everyone suspects the quietest guest.
A tall vertical spar rising from a ship's deck to carry sails, flags and radar.
A motorised four-wheeled vehicle designed to save time while regularly demanding trips to the garage.
A coastal tower flashing a warning beacon so ships don't confuse a rocky shore with a shortcut.
Thick mist or gloom that blurs the horizon and makes even weekend plans hard to read.
Golden nectar gathered and cured by bees — the only sweet treat backed by an entire winged workforce.
A powerful, thick-furred forest mammal that takes its winter sleep extremely seriously.
A narrow strip or furrow dividing neighbouring plots of land — and occasionally fuelling generations of arguments.
An unstable subatomic particle made of a quark and an antiquark that decays faster than you can pronounce its name.
A soft white limestone rock once used on classroom blackboards to dust teachers' sleeves.
A stick of coloured wax or chalk beloved by pavements and toddlers' palms.
A shallow sandbank lurking beneath the water, ready to halt even the most confident captain.
A standard unit of size or weight, or the sensible restraint often missing during shopping trips.
A castrated male horse, keeping all the strength and stamina with slightly less drama.
A standard template or measuring tool used to size things up accurately.
The central Eucharistic service of the Catholic Church, accompanied by centuries of sacred music.
A designated spot or chair — always worth claiming on public transport before someone else spots it.
Retaliation for a past wrong — a scheme that promises satisfaction while reliably creating fresh headaches.
Roughly four weeks on the calendar, or the celestial body orbiting Earth.
The simplest hydrocarbon and main ingredient of natural gas — everyday chemistry heating the kettle.
A small notch, tag or label used to tell your belongings apart from everyone else's.
An orderly, systematic way of tackling a problem — separating real work from frantic button-mashing.
A long-bladed weapon with a hilt — a historical argument that rarely needed follow-up questions.
A cherished ambition or mental movie you hope one day to turn into a documentary.
A large, sturdy bag of burlap or paper capable of swallowing everything from grain to moving-day clutter.
A split second — a blink of an eye brief enough to change everything.
A dark-shelled marine bivalve that clings to rocks and carries its own dining-room dish everywhere.
An imperial unit of distance equal to 1,609 metres on land — or 1,852 if you're measuring at sea.
A military engineer trained to lay or defuse mines — someone for whom 'watch your step' is never a figure of speech.
A musical key famed for sounding wistful or sad, or a person not yet legally an adult.
Freedom from war and conflict — or, in Russian, the entire world and universe rolled into one word.
An optical illusion caused by bent light rays, famously offering desert travellers lakes that vanish on approach.
A fragrant tree resin prized since antiquity for incense, perfume and biblical gifts.
An aromatic evergreen shrub with glossy leaves and white blossoms that smells unmistakably of the Mediterranean.
A deep, round dish built to hold soup, porridge or a very enthusiastic dog's dinner.
The process of cell division producing two identical daughter cells — biology's built-in Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V.
A shortened form of a word or phrase — saving ink, breath and precious seconds in text messages.
A reactive chemical element famous for glowing softly in the dark and lighting the tip of every matchstick.
The witty American sci-fi master behind 'Watchbird' and 'Mindswap', famed for satirical twists and cosmic irony.
A nautical map detailing coastlines, depths and hazards so ships don't have to find shallow reefs by feel.
A small circular opening drilled into a frozen lake by optimistic winter anglers.
A pair of parallel ski tracks pressed into the snow, carefully followed until someone tumbles into a drift.
A heavy, dark petroleum residue used in ships and boilers — guaranteed to ruin a white shirt on contact.
A miniature three-dimensional replica built to test a building, ship or aircraft before meeting full-sized bills.
A stocky, fluffy wild cat of the Asian steppes with a permanently grumpy expression, as if interrupted mid-nap.
A plump, spongy-pored woodland mushroom prized by foragers beneath pine and birch trees.
A towering industrial furnace that smelts iron ore around the clock at ferocious heat.
A formal reception room in a traditional home where guests are entertained — and footsteps echo politely.
A specific style and size of printed lettering, deciding whether a contract is readable or requires a magnifying glass.
A shrub or small tree bearing tart red berries, ideal for jams, compotes and savoury sauces.
The cartilaginous structure in the throat housing the vocal cords — famously prominent in men.
A light, airy baked cake layer forming the edible foundation for cream, jam and icing.
A small cone-shaped paper twist once used by shopkeepers to weigh out sweets and sunflower seeds.
A graceful female woodland deer sporting a white-spotted summer coat like natural camouflage.
The sturdy wheeled frame supporting an artillery cannon so it can be aimed and rolled into battle.
A single, nearly invisible nylon strand connecting a hopeful angler to whatever is lurking beneath the surface.
The cigar-smoking British statesman, writer and wartime Prime Minister who led the UK through WWII.
